subject: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — immediate customer impact & executive handoff
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@quantica.ai>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: High latency + 5xx surge in production (Quantica)

Michael / Marissa —

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and elevated 5xx rates hitting our dedicated pool starting ~08:40 UTC. At peak we're seeing tail latencies >1.2s and errors ramping to ~6% on generation calls. This is impacting our live inference SLA to customers.

Attached a short snapshot of metrics and a small error trace. We tried failover to the hosted variant but API keys returned 429 bursts. Can someone triage and advise immediate mitigations? This needs urgent handling; we have paying customers on the line.

Summary:
- Start: 2028-03-30 08:40 UTC
- Impact: 10% of requests delayed >500ms, 6% 5xx
- Affected model: ql-17b-chat (reserved pool)

Alex Romero
Head of ML Platform, Quantica Labs
attachments: metrics_snapshot_20280330.png, error_traces_excerpt.txt

From: michael.grant@redwood.ai
To: alex.romero@quantica.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-30T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx surge in production (Quantica)

Alex — thanks for the alert and the artifacts. We're on it. Quick status and immediate actions: 

1) Triage kickoff: Aditya will take lead to identify whether this is serving pressure (batching/prefix cache) or model-side instability.
2) Short-term mitigation: We can temporarily route a subset of Quantica traffic to a warm hosted fallback while we stabilize the reserved pool. Will need a signed short-term burst (ops) — Marissa, can pricing/credits be approved?
3) Customer comms: We'll send Quantica a short ETA and recommended mitigations in the next 30m.

Aditya — please post live findings in ALERT-7782 and include a rough cost for a 4-hour capacity burst. Marissa / Jonas — looping you for exec signal if we need immediate overcommit on the Dedicated cluster.

Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-30T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx surge in production (Quantica) — initial triage

Quick triage notes (10:00 UTC):
- Observed sustained queue growth on pool-dedicated-42 (ql-17b-chat pinned) beginning 08:42 UTC. CPU on host nodes nominal; GPU utilization trending 96-99% across a subset of nodes (hotspot).
- Continuous-batching window increased unexpectedly (~2.1x of baseline) due to a change in the client's request size distribution; KB cache hit-rate dropped (prefix mismatch) causing more full-sequence generation work.
- Error pattern: majority are internal timeouts between serving proxy and the model runtime (R11 / kv-cache timeout) rather than model OOMs.

Immediate mitigation options (technical):
A) Re-route 30% of production traffic to the hosted fallback model (latency trade-off ~+80ms but reliable).
B) Spin up two hot nodes from our burst pool (estimated 4-hour cost attached) — requires exec approval to exceed current reserved commit while we rebalance.
C) Temporarily lower batching window for this pool (reduces throughput but improves tail latencies).

I recommend doing A + C now, and B if we see persistent saturation after 30–45m. I've uploaded traces to ALERT-7782 and attached a cost estimate (proposed_burst_cost_estimate.pdf).

Aditya Rao
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
attachments: proposed_burst_cost_estimate.pdf

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, michael.grant@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Executive handoff: Quantica reserved throughput shortfall + recommended customer remediation

Jonas / Michael —

TL;DR: Quantica Labs is experiencing dedicated-pool saturation for their ql-17b-chat reservation causing customer-facing latency and errors. Engineering recommends immediate traffic split to hosted fallback + batching adjustment; ops is asking for a 4-hour capacity burst if saturation persists.

Customer posture: paying enterprise (annual commit, mid-Q4 renewal), high risk to ARR if incidents persist.
Business ask: approve one-time overcommit for up to 4 hours to stabilize the pool and avoid SLA penalties. Estimated incremental cost: see attached (approx $7.8k). Also propose offering Quantica a one-off goodwill credit on next invoice if they accept the temporary routing to hosted fallback.

Please advise: approve burst (yes/no) and any guidance on credits/contract exceptions. If approved, I'll coordinate PO/finance and our Marketplace capacity request immediately.

-Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_burst_cost_estimate.pdf

From: michael.grant@redwood.ai
To: alex.romero@quantica.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-30T18:03:00Z
Subject: Quantica — mitigation in place and next steps

Alex — thanks for your patience. Quick update on what we did and next steps: 

1) Immediate: We split 35% of Quantica production traffic to the hosted fallback at 11:32 UTC; observed tail latencies drop and 5xx rate fall from 6% -> 1.1% within 12 minutes.
2) Config change: lowered continuous-batching window on pool-dedicated-42 (applied 11:40 UTC) to reduce queuing; this reduced throughput but improved percentiles.
3) Capacity burst: Jonas approved a 3-hour hot-node burst. We spun up two hot nodes at 12:05 UTC; utilization stabilized to 68–75%. Burst cost estimate attached; Marissa will follow up on credits/finance.

Action items / timeline:
- Aditya: continue root-cause analysis — we still need to address prefix cache mismatch and a short-term model config that amplified batching.
- Marissa: confirm the goodwill credit and send customer's PO/invoice adjustment.
- Quantica: please run a small production test over next 24 hours and send any anomalous request examples.

We will keep this thread updated in ALERT-7782 and schedule a postmortem tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Apologies for the disruption; we're prioritizing stability and will provide a full RCA and remediation plan.

Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
